cme.note: Feature first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-09-03T01:37Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NNE in STEREO A COR2. This feature is likely outflow following CME: 2026-09-02T19:36Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

cme.note: Slow CME first seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-09-03T03:12Z. It is also seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. This feature is easiest to see in STEREO A COR2. The source may be related to some very faint field line movement best seen in SDO AIA 193 beginning as early as 2026-09-03T00:00Z centered around N50E40.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

cme.note: CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-09-03T04:48Z. It is also seen to the E in GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 but is covered by a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C3. The source is likely related to wide opening field lines beyond the E limb best seen in GOES SUVI 284 beginning as early as 2026-09-03T04:14Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 as well as on beyond-limb source location.

cme.note: CME first seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 starting at 2026-09-03T10:15Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and speculatively to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is a large filament eruption beyond the NE limb best seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2026-09-03T09:30Z

cmeAnalyses.note: This fit is more speculative than normal due to the faintness of the leading edge in STEREO A COR2. This CME is mostly missed by STEREO A COR2.

cme.note: Narrow CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-09-03T11:01Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. A possible source is a  C2.2 flare from AR 14523 (N11E44) seen peaking at 2026-09-03T09:42Z in SDO AIA 131, along with faint dimming seen in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

cme.note: CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There are two possible sources. The first possible source is a slow, gradual field line loop rising/opening seen in GOES SUVI 284 beginning at approx. 2026-09-03T14:00Z. The second potential source is a C6.9 flare from AR 14523 (N11E41) peaking at 2026-09-03T14:46Z as seen in SDO AIA 131. Based on triangulation of features, it is more likely the opening field lines seen in GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cme.note: Slow moving CME front visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery. It is overtaken by the CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-09-03T19:12Z. This CME may be associated with slow moving/opening field lines visible to the NE in GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky parameters using best fit of features in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery.

cme.note: Wide, slowly billowing CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. This CME overlaps and overtakes the CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 at 2026-09-03T18:00Z. The source for this CME is likely moving/opening field lines visible to the NE in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-09-03T18:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cme.note: CME visible to the E in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely moving/opening field lines visible beyond the E limb in GOES SUVI 284. This CME partially overlaps with the CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 at 2026-09-03T19:12Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on the best fit using SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cme.note: CME visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source of this CME is a filament eruption visible to the SE in GOES SUVI 304 with associated moving/opening field lines visible in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-09-03T21:56Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME deflects further south as it progresses outwards in the field of view.

cme.note: CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The CME is not visible in GOES CCOR-1 due to an outage. The source is likely AR 14524 (approximately N12E63). An eruption with moving field lines starting around 2026-09-04T05:09Z is best seen in SDO AIA 193 imagery. The eruption is not clearly seen in STEREO A EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT as well as the potential source location.

cme.note: CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-04T08:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This CME is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 due to a data gap which began at 2026-09-04T03:30Z. The source of this event is filament ejecta seen along the SE limb in GOES SUVI 304 beginning at approx. 2026-09-04T08:28Z, along with field line opening seen in GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

cme.note: CME visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The CME is obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3. The source is likely near the SE limb, as brightening and moving field lines are seen around S17E80 in SDO AIA 193 around 2026-09-04T12:42Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the potential source location using SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

cme.note: CME visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is an eruption near AR 14525, with several possible eruption candidates, including brightening and opening field lines seen starting around 2026-09-04T13:42Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the potential source location.

cme.note: Narrow, faint CME visible to the E in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely on or just beyond the E limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cme.note: Messy CME visible to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This CME is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery and there is a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 covering this event. The source for this CME may possibly be an eruption from AR 14524, however it is not clear.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit with possible source location of AR 14524 in mind.

cme.note: Fast CME visible to the E/SE in GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is a real-time DSN gap in the SOHO LASCO data covering the timing of this event. The source of this CME is a flare with associated filament eruption from AR 14524 (N12E55) starting around 2026-09-04T19:08Z as seen in GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

cme.note: This CME is visible to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is a real-time DSN gap in the SOHO LASCO data covering the timing of this event. The source of this CME is an eruption from beyond the E/NE limb with visible deflection to the NE starting around 2026-09-04T20:52Z as seen in GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

cme.note: This CME is visible to the southeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery and SOHO LASCO C2 imagery for a few frames before becoming too diffuse to observe. The source is likely an eruption centered near S18E15 as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-09-05T05:15Z. Dimming is observed east of the eruption site in SDO AIA 193/GOES SUVI 195 imagery, indicating possible eastern deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location, accounting for eastern deflection, and the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cme.note: This CME is visible to the east/southeast in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. This event is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 imagery in real time due to a data gap starting at 2026-09-05T03:30Z. The source is an eruption and C6.4 flare from Active Region 14524 (N12E45) starting around 2026-09-05T10:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cme.note: Bright CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and as a full halo in STEREO A COR2. The source is associated with an M1.0 flare from AR 14520 peaking at 2026-09-05T15:18Z, observed in SDO AIA 131. The eruption is additionally observed as field line movement, wide EUV wave, dimming, filament ejecta, and post-eruptive arcade/brightening in SDO AIA 171/193/211/304 starting at 2026-09-05T15:04Z. Observed in STEREO A EUVI 304 as brightening at 2026-09-05T15:15Z and STEREO A EUVI 195 as dimming at 2026-09-05T15:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SHOCK SOHO LASCO C2 only 3D analysis, using the source longitude at W68 as an estimate. With no COR2A available for triangulation at the time of analysis, parameters could vary slightly.

Updated BULK measurement based on updated imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. This updated measurement is pushed farther to the west to incorporate the leading edge feature in STEREO A COR2.
SOHO LASCO C2 only preliminary 3D analysis, using the source longitude at W68 as an estimate. With no COR2A available for triangulation yet, parameters could vary slightly.

cme.note: This CME is visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is related to an eruption and C8.5 flare from Active Region 14524 (N12E42) as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and GOES SUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-09-05T17:40Z. Dimming is observed south of the eruption site in SDO AIA 193/GOES SUVI 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

cme.note: Narrow CME first seen to the ENE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-09-05T22:00Z. It is also seen to the ENE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NE in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely a filament eruption near the E limb best seen in SDO AIA 304 starting around 2026-09-05T21:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

cme.note: This CME is visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery only. This event is not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 in real-time due to data gaps starting around 2206-09-06T03:30Z. The source is likely related to an eruption from Active Region 14524 (N12E34) starting around 2026-09-06T06:55Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the source location. Due to a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery, a triangulated measurement was not available. The measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

cme.note: This CME is visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery only. This event is not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 in real-time due to data gaps starting around 2206-09-06T03:30Z. The source is an eruption and C5.0 flare from Active Region 14524 (N12E32) starting around 2026-09-06T10:36Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery. An EUV wave and subsequent dimming is observed moving south of the eruption site, seen in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the source location. Due to a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery, a triangulated measurement was not available. The measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

cme.note: Very faint feature seen only seen to the NE part way into the FOV of STEREO A COR2 after a data gap ending at 2026-09-06T21:53Z. A possible source candidate is a small amount of ejecta seen over the ENE limb in SDO AIA 304 beginning around 2026-09-06T18:35Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to single coronagraph perspective and beyond-limb source candidate.

cme.note: This CME is visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery, and to the west in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is far-sided and likely related to an opening of field lines visible over eastern limb in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery starting around 2026-09-07T00:50Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cme.note: This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1 (partially obscured by the pylon), and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a slow-to-lift-off filament eruption visible over the northwest limb in SDO AIA 171/304 and GOES SUVI 171/284/304 imagery starting around 2026-09-06T22:00Z. This same filament is visible lifting off north of disk center as seen in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cme.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be related to an eruption from Active Region 14524 (N12E22) starting around 2026-09-07T08:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. Dimming is observed north of the eruption site in SDO AIA 193 imagery, with an opening of field lines visible over the northeast limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery, indicating northern deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cme.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a C2.4 flare from Active Region 14521 (N10W35) starting around 2026-09-08T12:20Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cme.note: Faint, narrow CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. It is not clearly seen in available GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source of this CME appears to be a filament eruption best seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 and 195 as well as GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2026-09-09T06:52Z. There is a dimming signature visible in STEREO A EUVI 195 that appears to "pinch" towards the filament before it lifts off.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cme.note: This CME is faintly seen to the East in STEREO A COR2 imagery. It appears to be associated with a C3.4 flare (caught in GOES-S) peaking at 2026-09-09T09:08Z (occurs during an eclipse in GOES-P) from AR 14524 (N15W05). This CME is very slow and not clearly seen in the SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is a simultaneous CME visible to the East in SOHO LASCO C2 around the same time, however this CME is believed to be associated with a slow farsided filament eruption and is not the same CME feature seen in STEREO A that is associated with this entry.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on potential source location and best fit in STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cme.note: This CME is visible to the East in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A imagery. The source of this CME appears to be a long-duration filament eruption visible along the E/SE limb in GOES SUVI 304 and 284 imagery starting around 2026-09-09T06:30Z with liftoff around 2026-09-09T10:36Z. Moving/opening field lines are visible with some apparent deflection towards the north as it progresses out of the field of view in GOES SUVI 284. The CME also exhibits a small deflection towards the north as it progresses outward in the SOHO LASCO field of view. There is a simultaneous CME visible to the East in STEREO A COR2 around the same start time, however this CME is believed to be associated with a C-class flare and is not the same CME feature seen in SOHO LASCO C2 that is associated with this entry. The CME is visible in later frames in STEREO A as a wider feature.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cme.note: CME first seen to East by GOES CCOR-1 beginning at 2026-09-09T21:45Z. This event is not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-09-09T22:24Z or in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-09-09T21:23Z. The source of this event is field line opening seen along the SE limb in GOES SUVI 284 beginning at approx. 2026-09-09T21:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using a longitude of E90 due to source on or beyond the East limb and lack of coronagraph imagery to triangulate.
